title: Relative finite alteration diagrams descend and admit close section models
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local ring with separably closed residue field $k$, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, and fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $A$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\widehat S=\varprojlim_\alpha S_\alpha$ be a small cofiltered affine system over $S$ with local maps, each $S_\alpha$ a strict localization of a smooth finite-type $S$-scheme at a point with residue field $k$, and all closed residue field maps equal to $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $Y\hookrightarrow\widehat S$ be a reduced closed subscheme, $U\subseteq Y$ an affine open, and $P_\bullet\to Y$ a hypercover through a finite degree $L$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations; this means an augmented simplicial diagram in $\operatorname{alt}/Y$ with covering matching maps [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Include any specified finite diagram of finite-type schemes, morphisms, closed subschemes, functions on affine charts and equalities involving $Y,U,P_0,\ldots,P_L$. After restricting to sufficiently large indices this entire diagram has compatible models over $S_\alpha$, with $Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow S_\alpha$ closed and $U_\alpha\subseteq Y_\alpha$ affine open. The diagrams $P_{\bullet,\alpha}\to Y_\alpha$ are truncated hypercovers in $\operatorname{alt}/Y_\alpha$, and their ordinary pullbacks to $Y$ recover the specified finite diagram (in particular the specified hypercover, which is already reduced and dominant). Their closed fibres identify with the original closed fibres. There are an index $\alpha_0$ and an integer $n_0\geq1$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$ and every $S$-section $u:S\to S_\alpha$ agreeing with $\widehat S\to S_\alpha$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{n_0}$, the dominant reduced pullbacks of $P_{\bullet,\alpha}$ form a truncated hypercover of $Y_u=Y_\alpha\times_{S_\alpha,u}S$. Here dominant reduced pullback is the reduced union of the components of the ordinary fibre product dominating components of the new base; its levels have finite generic fibres over that base. The model diagram, including its closed subschemes, functions and equalities, pulls back by ordinary scheme fibre products before this dominant reduction [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: XV 3.2.1–3.2.3 and 3.3.1, printed pp.222–224; II 3.2.1 standard covering refinements and III 3.1(i),(iii), 3.1.1, printed pp.37–38, for retaining generic-finiteness and covering certificates in close models. Relative finite-diagram version over the closed model Y, with all matching objects and their covering certificates included; no regularity, boundary or dimension assertion.
